name: Mulberry
scientific: Morus rubra (red mulberry); Morus alba (white mulberry, naturalized)
habitat: Red mulberry in rich woods and bottomlands of the eastern US; white mulberry naturalized nearly everywhere in old fields, urban lots, alleys, roadsides and forest edges, including throughout the West and Great Plains where it was planted by the million for windbreaks.
parts: Fully ripe fruit only, raw or in pies, jams and syrups. Ripe means deep purple-black (or, on white-fruited trees, soft and translucent) and dropping at a touch. Unripe fruit and the milky white sap that runs from every part of the tree cause stomach upset and, per NC State, hallucinations; the sap can also cause contact dermatitis. Ripe fruit is harmless.
harvest: Spread a sheet or tarp under the tree and shake — this is far easier than picking and takes only what is truly ripe. Mulberry (especially naturalized white mulberry, a listed invasive in Wisconsin, Indiana and Ohio) fruits so heavily that over-harvest is not a concern; the fruit is a major bird food, and the tree drops far more than anyone can gather.
